ABOUT THE GUIDE

Good recommendations
start with the details.

We help people choose gifts for pilots and aviation enthusiasts, even when they don’t know the difference between a headset plug and a kneeboard.

How we choose

We look for a clear match between a product and a recipient. Our research considers the intended use, price, compatibility, useful features and reasons a gift might be wrong for someone. We use published manufacturer and retailer information; we do not claim hands-on testing, personal product experience or independent customer reviews.

One product, one set of facts

Our shared research library currently contains 62 products. Each record includes its model, source, photograph, price-check date, intended recipient, strengths, limitations and compatibility notes. Guides draw from these records and explain the choice for their particular reader. Not every researched product is recommended in every guide, and library inclusion is not a performance award.

Our relationship with ATC

Pilot Gift Guide is produced by the team behind ATC, the airport-listening app. We include our own app where it fits the topic and disclose this relationship beside the recommendation. Other featured brands have not sponsored these guides, and we have not added third-party affiliate tracking to retailer links.

Prices, variants and availability

Prices are observations from the dates shown beside each recommendation, in US dollars before tax and shipping. A price can apply to a specific plug, size or configuration. Source pages remain the place to confirm current stock, specifications, delivery, subscription terms and returns. This website does not sell products or accept orders.

Photography

Product photographs come from the linked manufacturer and retailer listings and remain their property. Product arrangements are illustrations, not evidence of a hands-on test. Aviation photography: Cody F, Nick Morales, ALPEN AIR, Tomas Martinez, via Unsplash.

Flying equipment needs a personal check

Our gift advice is not flight instruction or operational guidance. Confirm equipment requirements with the pilot and, where relevant, their instructor or employer.
